request: what is the slope of y = x^2 at x = 1?

beats.intent: Axes with the parabola y = x^2 from -2 to 2
beats.narration: Here is the parabola y equals x squared.
beats.code:
stage.title("Slope at a point")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(-2, 2), y_range=(0, 4))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: x ** 2, label="y = x^2")

beats.intent: A secant from x = 1 to x = 3 shrinking onto the tangent at x = 1, its slope read out
beats.narration: Take a secant from one to a nearby point and slide the second point in. Its slope settles on two.
beats.code:
secant_to_tangent(stage, ax, lambda x: x ** 2, 1, h=1)
stage.caption("The secant's slope settles at 2")

beats.intent: The point (1, 1) marked with the equation dy/dx = 2x = 2 beside the graph
beats.narration: The derivative two x gives the same answer: at x equals one, the slope is two.
beats.code:
p = mark_point(stage, ax, 1, 1, label="(1, 1)")
stage.equation(r"\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x", r"2 \cdot 1 = 2")

request: what is the integral of x from 0 to 4 as an area?

beats.intent: Axes with the line y = x from 0 to 4
beats.narration: Draw the line y equals x.
beats.code:
stage.title("Integral as area")
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 5), y_range=(0, 5))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: x, label="y = x")

beats.intent: The triangle under the line from 0 to 4 shaded
beats.narration: The integral from zero to four is the area under it: a triangle.
beats.code:
shade_area(stage, ax, g, 0, 4)
stage.caption("The area under the line up to 4")

beats.intent: The shaded triangle with the equation ∫ x dx from 0 to 4 = ½ · 4 · 4 = 8
beats.narration: Half of base times height: half of four times four is eight.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\int_0^4 x\,dx", r"= \tfrac12 \cdot 4 \cdot 4 = 8")

request: which total is most likely when you roll two dice?

beats.intent: The 6 by 6 grid of two-dice outcomes with the six ways to make 7 lit
beats.narration: Two dice give thirty six equally likely outcomes. Six of them add to seven.
beats.code:
stage.title("Two dice")
cells = draw_dice_grid(stage, highlight_sum=7)
stage.caption("6 of 36 outcomes make 7")

beats.intent: Bars of how many ways each total from 2 to 12 can happen, peaking at 7
beats.narration: Count the ways for every total: one, two, three, up to six for seven, and back down.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
bars = draw_bars(stage, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1], labels=list(range(2, 13)))
highlight(stage, bars[5])

beats.intent: The tall middle bar beside the equation P(7) = 6/36 = 1/6
beats.narration: So seven comes up one time in six, more than any other total.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"P(7) = \frac{6}{36} = \frac16")

request: a probability tree for flipping a coin twice

beats.intent: A tree with a start node branching to H and T
beats.narration: The first flip splits into heads or tails, each with probability one half.

beats.intent: Each of H and T branching again to four leaves HH, HT, TH, TT
beats.narration: Each branch splits again, giving four outcomes.
beats.code:
nodes2 = dict(nodes, HH=(0.6, 0.8), HT=(0.6, 0.25), TH=(0.6, -0.25), TT=(0.6, -0.8))
dots2, lines2 = draw_network(stage, nodes2, [("start", "H"), ("start", "T"), ("H", "HH"), ("H", "HT"), ("T", "TH"), ("T", "TT")])

beats.intent: The HH leaf highlighted with the equation P(HH) = ½ × ½ = ¼
beats.narration: Multiply along the branches: two heads has probability a quarter.
beats.code:
highlight(stage, dots2["HH"])
stage.equation(r"P(HH) = \tfrac12 \times \tfrac12 = \tfrac14")

request: what does the matrix [[1, 2], [0, 1]] do to the plane?

beats.intent: A grid with i-hat and j-hat
beats.narration: Start with the grid and the two basis arrows.

stage.title("A shear")
p = draw_plane(stage)
i_hat, j_hat = draw_basis(stage, p)

beats.intent: The matrix [[1, 2], [0, 1]] applied, j-hat sliding to (2, 1) while i-hat stays
beats.narration: Apply the matrix. i-hat stays where it is; j-hat slides over to two, one.

beats.intent: The sheared grid beside the matrix written out with its columns
beats.narration: The columns of the matrix are exactly where the basis arrows landed.

request: why do angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees?

beats.intent: A straight line with a ray from its middle making two angles
beats.narration: Draw a straight line and a ray from a point on it.
beats.code:
stage.title("Angles on a line")
base = draw_line(stage, (-3, -1), (3, -1))
ray = draw_line(stage, (0, -1), (1.5, 1.6), color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The two angles marked with arcs, 60 degrees and 120 degrees
beats.narration: The ray splits the straight angle into two: here sixty degrees and one hundred and twenty.
beats.code:
a1 = Angle(Line((0, -1, 0), (3, -1, 0)), Line((0, -1, 0), (1.5, 1.6, 0)), radius=0.6, color=GREEN)
a2 = Angle(Line((0, -1, 0), (1.5, 1.6, 0)), Line((0, -1, 0), (-3, -1, 0)), radius=0.8, color=RED)
stage.play(Create(a1), Create(a2))
stage.label(a1, "60°", direction=RIGHT, color=GREEN)
stage.label(a2, "120°", direction=UP, color=RED)

beats.intent: The equation 60° + 120° = 180° beside the figure
beats.narration: Together they make the straight line, half a turn: one hundred and eighty degrees.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"60^\circ + 120^\circ = 180^\circ")

request: quicksort: splitting a list around a pivot

beats.intent: Seven bars 5, 2, 8, 1, 9, 3, 7 with the last, 7, as the pivot
beats.narration: Pick the last number, seven, as the pivot.
beats.code:
stage.title("Partition around a pivot")
bars = draw_array(stage, [5, 2, 8, 1, 9, 3, 7])
highlight(stage, bars[6], color=RED)

beats.intent: Bars swapped so everything smaller than 7 moves left: 5, 2, 1, 3 then 8, 9
beats.narration: Walk along the list and swap every number smaller than seven to the front.

swap_bars(stage, bars, 2, 3)
swap_bars(stage, bars, 3, 5)

stage.caption("7 is now in its final place")

request: how big is the angle in each corner of a regular hexagon?

beats.intent: A regular hexagon
beats.narration: A regular hexagon has six equal sides and six equal angles.
beats.code:
stage.title("The hexagon's angles")
pts = [(2 * np.cos(TAU * k / 6), 2 * np.sin(TAU * k / 6)) for k in range(6)]
hexa = draw_polygon(stage, pts, where=None)

beats.intent: Lines from one corner splitting the hexagon into 4 triangles
beats.narration: From one corner, three diagonals split it into four triangles.
beats.code:
d1 = draw_line(stage, pts[0], pts[2], dashed=True)
d2 = draw_line(stage, pts[0], pts[3], dashed=True)
d3 = draw_line(stage, pts[0], pts[4], dashed=True)
stage.caption("4 triangles")

beats.intent: The equation 4 × 180° = 720°, 720° ÷ 6 = 120° beside the hexagon
beats.narration: Four triangles give seven hundred and twenty degrees, shared by six corners: one hundred and twenty each.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"4 \times 180^\circ = 720^\circ", r"720^\circ \div 6 = 120^\circ")

request: what does an Archimedean spiral look like?

beats.intent: Axes with a dot starting at the origin
beats.narration: A point starts at the centre.
beats.code:
stage.title("An Archimedean spiral")
p = draw_plane(stage)
o = mark_point(stage, p, (0, 0))

beats.intent: The spiral r = 0.4θ traced out over three turns
beats.narration: It turns at a steady rate while moving outward at a steady rate: the distance grows in step with the angle.
beats.code:
spiral = ParametricFunction(lambda t: p.c2p(0.12 * t * np.cos(t), 0.12 * t * np.sin(t)), t_range=[0, 6 * PI], color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(spiral), run_time=3)
stage.add(spiral)

beats.intent: Arrows showing equal gaps between neighbouring turns
beats.narration: So each turn sits the same distance outside the last one.
beats.code:
g1 = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(0.12 * 2 * PI, 0), p.c2p(0.12 * 4 * PI, 0))
g2 = draw_arrow(stage, p.c2p(0.12 * 4 * PI, 0), p.c2p(0.12 * 6 * PI, 0))
stage.caption("Equal gaps between the turns")

request: what does multiplying a vector by a matrix do, step by step?

stage.title("Matrix times vector")
p = draw_plane(stage)
v = draw_vector(stage, p, (1, 2), label="v")

beats.intent: The matrix [[2, 0], [1, 1]] applied, v riding along to (2, 3)
beats.narration: Apply the matrix with columns two, one and zero, one. The vector rides along and lands at two, three.

request: how does a clock show 3 o'clock as an angle?

beats.intent: A clock face as a circle with 12 tick dots
beats.narration: A clock face: twelve hours around a full circle of three hundred and sixty degrees.
beats.code:
stage.title("Angles on a clock")
face = draw_circle(stage, radius=2)
ticks = VGroup(*[Dot(face.get_center() + 1.8 * np.array([np.sin(TAU * k / 12), np.cos(TAU * k / 12), 0]), radius=0.05) for k in range(12)])
stage.play(FadeIn(ticks))

beats.intent: Two hands from the centre pointing to 12 and to 3
beats.narration: At three o'clock the hands point to twelve and to three.
beats.code:
c = face.get_center()
m_hand = draw_arrow(stage, c, c + np.array([0, 1.6, 0]))
h_hand = draw_arrow(stage, c, c + np.array([1.2, 0, 0]))

beats.intent: The right angle between the hands marked 90°
beats.narration: Three hours out of twelve is a quarter turn: ninety degrees.
beats.code:
ang = RightAngle(Line(c, c + UP), Line(c, c + RIGHT), length=0.4, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(ang))
stage.equation(r"\frac{3}{12} \times 360^\circ = 90^\circ")

request: the area of a trapezium as the average of its sides times its height

beats.intent: A trapezium with parallel sides 2 and 6 and height 3
beats.narration: A trapezium with parallel sides two and six, three apart.
beats.code:
stage.title("Area of a trapezium")
trap = draw_polygon(stage, [(-3, -1.5), (3, -1.5), (1, 1.5), (-1, 1.5)])
stage.caption("Parallel sides 2 and 6, height 3")

beats.intent: A copy of the trapezium turned upside down beside it, making a parallelogram
beats.narration: Put a copy upside down next to it and the two make a parallelogram with base eight.
beats.code:
copy = trap.copy().set_color(GREEN)
stage.play(copy.animate.rotate(PI).next_to(trap, RIGHT, buff=-2.0), run_time=1.5)
stage.add(copy)

beats.intent: The equation Area = ½ (2 + 6) × 3 = 12 beside the shapes
beats.narration: The parallelogram is eight times three, twenty four, so one trapezium is half: twelve.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\text{Area} = \tfrac12 (2 + 6) \times 3", r"= 12")
